conventions.convention: Quantizers use the relative Borel sigma algebra on a Borel subset of Euclidean space, a probability measure with finite second moment, and a finite discrete index alphabet. Nearest-center ties go to the least index; coincident centers and empty cells are permitted.

Indexed data have strictly positive weights summing to one. Lloyd updates nonempty clusters to weighted centroids, retains empty-cluster centers, and stops when the ordered center tuple is unchanged. Arithmetic and comparisons are exact.

Exhaustive search enumerates all k^N indexed assignments lexicographically, uses x_1 for empty-cluster centers, retains the first minimum-cost assignment, and returns its centers with the least-index nearest-center assignment.
The cumulative point density is positive, normalized, and C1 on a fixed nondegenerate compact interval; its integrals are ordinary Riemann integrals of continuous functions.

Both source and point densities are positive normalized C1 functions on the same compact interval. Compander boundaries are inverse cumulative images of j/N, reproductions are images of (j−1/2)/N, and cells are left-closed and right-open except for the final cell containing b. These cells need not be nearest-center cells.
C2 regularity of the cumulative inverse includes one-sided derivatives at the endpoints.

load_bearing.statement: For a nonempty indexed cluster S with positive weights, total weight W_S and weighted centroid μ_S, its cost at c equals its cost at μ_S plus W_S‖c−μ_S‖². Consequently μ_S is the unique minimizer. An empty cluster has zero cost for every center.
For a<b and positive normalized C1 g on [a,b], G_g is a strictly increasing C2 bijection onto [0,1]. Its inverse φ is C2, with one-sided endpoint derivatives, and φ′=1/(g∘φ), φ″=−(g′∘φ)/(g∘φ)³.
Let a<b and let f,g:[a,b]→(0,∞) be C1 probability densities. For the specified compact compander, lim as N→∞ of N²D_N(f,g) equals (1/12)∫_a^b f(x)/g(x)² dx.
Under the finite squared-error quantizer hypotheses, the least-index nearest-center rule defines a Borel quantizer with finite distortion. Coincident centers and empty cells are allowed.

published_dependencies.used_for: Existence and differentiation of cumulative integrals; endpoint evaluation of primitives; the two changes of variable in the high-rate proof.
Strict increase of the cumulative coordinate, inverse derivative quotients, endpoint derivative extensions, uniform Taylor remainder estimates, and midpoint-sum convergence.
Differentiation of reciprocal and quotient expressions in the inverse-regularity and high-rate proofs.
Interior differentiation of composed scalar functions in inverse regularity, integral substitutions, high-rate estimates, and admissibility of the optimal density.
Positive minima of positive continuous densities and finite uniform bounds on compact intervals.
Surjectivity of the continuous cumulative map onto [0,1].
Uniform continuity of H in the midpoint-sum convergence argument.
Meaning of positive cube roots and fractional powers in point-density optimization.
Continuity and differentiability of f^(1/3), ensuring the proposed optimal point density belongs to the admissible class.

concerns.concern: The cell-schematic prose writes the cumulative inverse as "$phi(u)=u$". The missing backslash renders three separate mathematical letters instead of the φ used throughout the definitions and proofs.

seams_checked.note: Read both page interfaces and the actual draft supplier def-it-single-letter-distortion-and-block-distortion. The quantizer definition specializes its measurable nonnegative distortion to squared Euclidean error and its expected single-letter criterion to n=1. This preserves the supplier's normalization and expected-versus-excess distinction. The prerequisite page makes no reverse claim about this batch, and no rate-distortion coding theorem is imported into the finite optimization or compact asymptotic proofs.
